title: Canonical extension presentation of an etale torsor
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G$ an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $T$ a $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor]. A canonical extension presentation consists of an abelian sheaf $E$, a morphism $i:G\to E$, a natural family $j_U:T(U)\to E(U)$ satisfying $j_U(g\cdot t)=j_U(t)+i_U(g)$, and a morphism $p:E\to\mathbf Z_S$ satisfying $pi=0$ and $p_U(j_U(t))=1$. The quotient universal property is required: for every abelian sheaf $A$, morphism $k:G\to A$, and natural family $a_U:T(U)\to A(U)$ with $a_U(g\cdot t)=a_U(t)+k_U(g)$, there is a unique morphism $l:E\to A$ with $li=k$ and $l_U(j_U(t))=a_U(t)$ for every object $U$ and section $t$. Thus the specified quotient is $(G\oplus\mathbf Z[T])/\langle j(g\cdot t)-j(t)-i(g)\rangle$, with its augmentation to the sheafification of the constant integer presheaf.
